howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

Port Orange is one of Volusia County's fastest-growing family communities, just south of Daytona Beach along the Dunlawton Avenue corridor. Here's exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Port Orange?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate Port Orange license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Port Orange a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes. Port Orange is a steady, family-oriented suburb with strong schools and consistent demand from buyers moving within Volusia County and relocating from out of state. It's mostly mainland single-family housing, the kind of repeat, referral-driven business a new agent can build a career on. Across Volusia County, roughly 900 homes sell each month at about a $343,000 median, and rising inventory means more listings to work.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight. Sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area's largest brokerage since 1963, with a Port Orange office on Dunlawton Avenue and around 300 agents across Volusia and Flagler County. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
